title: Global debt strains elevate yield floors as RBI drains liquidity ahead of H2 issuance
changed: Global sovereign debt dynamics hardened as the IMF warned of unsustainable fiscal paths in the US and UK, reinforced by an August borrowing surge in Britain and a US Q2 current account deficit widening 15.7% to $246 billion. With European Central Bank Chief Economist Lane signaling sluggish euro area growth and steady rates, and Japan core CPI hovering near 2% to restrain Bank of Japan hikes, developed market yields remained underpinned, providing persistent support to the US dollar.

Domestic fixed income benchmarks adjusted to heavy primary paper as the government outlined ₹7.86 lakh crore in H2 bond sales, moderating the full-year target while state governments absorbed over ₹38,000 crore across successive auctions. The Reserve Bank of India anchored short-term funding benchmarks by pricing 1-year T-bills at 6.00%—a 61 bps spread over 3-month paper—and fixed the GoI Floating Rate Bond 2033 coupon at 6.87% for H2 FY27.

The RBI moved aggressively to sterilize surplus domestic liquidity, conducting a ₹25,000 crore OMO bond sale that drew a 3.4x bid cover alongside daily VRRR operations that absorbed up to ₹1.01 lakh crore at 5.24%. These drains anchored the weighted average overnight money market rate at 5.08% ahead of quarter-end funding adjustments, while the Ways and Means Advances limit for October to March was established at ₹50 trillion.

From a regulatory and balance sheet perspective, the RBI revised market risk guidelines to alter trading book capital charge computations across interest rate, equity, and foreign exchange portfolios. Parallel actions finalized OTC derivative novation directions, amended portfolio valuation rules for All India Financial Institutions, and tightened trade reporting under FEMA, directly raising capital calibration and audit standards across bank books.

threads.name: Global sovereign debt term premium
threads.note: IMF debt warnings and widening US twin deficits maintain upward pressure on developed-market benchmark yields. Downward surprises in growth data confirm this yield floor, while synchronized fiscal consolidation breaks it.

threads.name: RBI systemic liquidity sterilization
threads.note: Consecutive VRRR operations at 5.24% and the ₹25,000 crore OMO sale reflect direct efforts to keep overnight money market rates near the policy floor. Persistent credit-deposit divergence noted in the RBI bulletin will determine whether systemic liquidity transitions into a deficit.

threads.name: Shifting Indian capital flows
threads.note: Q1 FY27 FDI equity inflows rose 6% to $19.8 billion despite a 76% contraction in direct US flows, shifting funding dependence toward trade export strength. A sharp widening in the merchandise trade balance breaks this balance-of-payments buffer.

threads.name: Bank trading book compliance overhaul
threads.note: Standardized market risk capital charges and revised valuation frameworks for financial institutions alter bank capital ratios. Audit adherence depends on clearing member implementation under SEBI and RBI reporting platforms.
